title: Scalable Multitask Learning Using Gradient-based Estimation of Task Affinity

problem.claim: Multitask learning requires modeling relationships among tasks, including pairwise and higher-order task affinity.

gap.claim: Existing naive computation of pairwise or higher-order task affinity requires repeated training over task combinations, making it computationally intensive.

contributions.claim: The paper presents Grad-TAG, an algorithm for estimating task affinities without repeated training on pooled task combinations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Grad-TAG as a new algorithm.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multitask learning is used to train models across diverse tasks.
Task affinity models relationships among tasks, including pairwise and higher-order relationships.
Naive affinity computation is computationally intensive because it repeatedly trains on different task combinations.
Grad-TAG is introduced to estimate task affinities without repeated training.

unknowns: No empirical results, datasets, baselines, or quantitative performance are stated.
The abstract does not specify the accuracy, computational savings, or scalability conditions of Grad-TAG.
No limitations, failure cases, or applicability boundaries are stated.
